questions.prompt: Why is client-side validation not a substitute for server-side authorization?
options: Server-side code cannot access request data.
Client validation always uses encrypted input.
A user can modify or bypass client code; trusted permissions must be enforced server-side.
questions.explanation: The client improves feedback, but the server must independently enforce access and business rules.

questions.prompt: When rendering untrusted user-provided plain text, what should be avoided?
options: Interpreting it as HTML with innerHTML without a suitable sanitization/trust policy.
Validating data at the server boundary.
questions.explanation: HTML injection can turn untrusted strings into markup; safe rendering and contextual validation reduce risk.
